rationale: dual_domain_n2i-claude-agentic: train_n=200, val_n=24, batch_size=1, grad_clip=0.3, seed=42, warm_start=True, pretrain_epochs=6, n_iter=300, outer_wall_s=1700, lr=0.0001, unet_c=16, rationale=iter-18 (REDISPATCH after job 765177 TIMED OUT at 28:45 without recording): HYPOTHESIS KNOB = n_iter 600 -> 300 (HALVE per-scan Adam steps), at the iter-17 recorded config on the val_n=24 basis (val_n=24/ep/lr1e-4/warm_start=True/unet_c16/seed42/grad_clip0.3). This is BOTH the wall fix AND a clean less-per-scan-overfit probe. PREVIOUS RECORDED RESULT (iter-17, grad_clip 1.0->0.3): val_ssim 0.45779, hr 0.0005, PSNR 13.45 -- in the 0.43-0.47 band, FLAT vs the iter-13 seed42/val_n24 baseline 0.4616 (inside the documented val_n=24 4-seed noise floor std 0.0143); best ever is still iter-5 0.50811 (hr0). FAILURE MODE = the 0.466 M-param U-Net OVERFITS each single noisy 128-view sparse-phantom scan in the no-early-stop _fit_one_scene loop (the 6-param bilateral twin physically CANNOT overfit, hr+0.33; this U-Net stays hr~0 at 0.43-0.51 SSIM); the per-image fit is FBP-bounded AND has a large init-driven stochastic noise floor (well-documented). LEVER CHOICE: campaign-state says raising n_iter HURTS (per-scan overfit: demo 0.4785->0.4293 @n_iter1200) and that fewer steps anchored nearer the warm-start init can help -- so LOWERING n_iter 600->300 is a clean less-overfit probe that has NOT been tried, and it ALSO directly fixes the wall (halves the dominant per-image cost). KEPT FIXED (settled, do NOT touch): warm_start=True (LOAD-BEARING-POSITIVE, iter-8 off -0.0595), lr=1e-4 (iter-3/iter-9 bracket as per-scan optimum), val_n=24 (the stable comparison basis -- NOT reduced, same metric basis as iter-13..17), grad_clip=0.3 (iter-17 recorded value), unet_c=16, seed=42 (peak basin). HYPOTHESIS: if per-scan U-Net overfitting (not the FBP bound) holds SSIM below the iter-5 0.508 peak, halving n_iter keeps each per-scan fit anchored nearer the good warm-start init, lifting the val_n=24 seed42 mean above the iter-13/iter-17 ~0.46 reads toward 0.508. FALSIFIER: if SSIM stays in the 0.43-0.47 band (within noise of iter-17 0.4578), the floor is the FBP bound itself, FINALIZING the structural ceiling for the iter-20 writeup. hr expected ~0 either way (structurally FBP-bounded on dense 128-view phantoms). BUDGET CUT (NOT the hypothesis): pretrain_epochs 12 -> 6 PURELY to guarantee the wall. The PRIOR iter-18 attempt (job 765177) ran the full 16800-step budget (warm 12x200=2400 + per-image 24x600=14400) and was KILLED at 28:45 by the sbatch wall WITHOUT recording. ep6 is a documented strong warm-start init (iter-4 ep6 0.4957, near the ep12 0.5081 peak), so this budget cut costs little init quality while halving the pre-pass cost. WALL: new step budget = warm 6x200=1200 + per-image 24x300=7200 = 8400 steps (vs the 16800 that timed out); at the iter-17 effective rate ~0.088 s/step this is ~740 s ~= 12.4 min, and even on a slow node (~0.10-0.11 s/step) ~840-925 s ~= 14-15.5 min, with outer_wall_s=1700 as a hard internal guard that aborts cleanly under the 00:30:00 (1800 s) sbatch wall so the iter RECORDS even on a pathological node. All recon-affecting knobs IDENTICAL to the iter-17 recorded config EXCEPT n_iter 600->300 (hypothesis) and pretrain_epochs 12->6 (budget cut).

rationale: dual_domain_n2i-claude-agentic: train_n=200, val_n=24, batch_size=1, grad_clip=0.3, seed=42, warm_start=True, pretrain_epochs=12, n_iter=600, outer_wall_s=1700, lr=0.0001, unet_c=16, rationale=iter-17: ONE knob -> grad_clip 1.0 -> 0.3 (TIGHTER per-step gradient-norm cap), at the iter-5 PEAK family config on the val_n=24 basis (val_n=24/ep12/lr1e-4/warm_start=True/n_iter600/unet_c16/seed42). FIRST ceiling-RAISER attempt since iter-5 (0.50811 hr0, the run best); iters 6-16 never beat it (iters 13-16 were val_n=24 noise-floor reads: seed42=0.4616 / seed123=0.4431 / seed7=0.4257 / seed2024=0.4379, 4-seed mean 0.4421 std 0.0143, hr 0 throughout). DIAGNOSIS (numbers, not pixels): iter-16 (seed7->2024) SSIM 0.43794 PSNR 13.95 hr0; best ever = iter-5 0.50811 (seed42/ep12/lr1e-4/val_n6). FAILURE MODE = the 0.466 M-param U-Net OVERFITS each single noisy 128-view sparse-phantom scan in the no-early-stop _fit_one_scene loop (the 6-param bilateral twin physically CANNOT overfit, which is why the twin clears baseline at hr+0.33 while this U-Net stays hr~0 at 0.43-0.51 SSIM); the per-image fit is FBP-bounded AND has a large init-driven stochastic noise floor (now well-documented). EXHAUSTED / FORBIDDEN recon axes (do NOT retry, per handoff): n_iter (iter-2 1200 steps 0.4785->0.4293, per-scan overfit), warm_start (iter-8 off -0.0595, load-bearing-positive), pretrain_epochs (ep12 peak, ep18 worse 0.5016), lr (iter-3 1e-3->1e-4 + iter-9 1e-4->2e-4 bracket 1e-4 as the per-scan optimum), unet_c (design-doc warned-against; mayo n2i c16->c32 flat 0.9508). val_n is a noise-floor-READ axis (6->12->24), not a recon lever. LEVER CHOICE (the one genuinely-untried ALLOWED knob value): grad_clip 1.0 -> 0.3. grad_clip is applied as clip_grad_norm_(params, gc) in BOTH the warm-start pre-pass (solver lines 263-264) and the per-scan Adam loop (lines 137-138). LOWERING it tightens the per-step gradient-norm cap, which ANCHORS each per-scan fit more tightly near the good warm-start init across all 600 steps -- directly attacking the named per-scan-overfitting failure mode. Lowering can NEVER trigger the 2304/128-view FBP-adjoint overflow the guard exists to prevent (it only REDUCES gradient magnitude), so it is both SAFE and on-mandate; prior iters deliberately declined RAISING grad_clip, but LOWERING it has never been tried. Reset to the seed42 PEAK basin (the good basin, not the iter-16 seed2024 basin) so the grad_clip contrast is clean against the iter-13 seed42/val_n24 read (0.4616). HYPOTHESIS: if per-scan U-Net overfitting (not the FBP bound) is what holds SSIM below the iter-5 0.508 peak, the tighter clip keeps Adam pinned near the warm-start init, lifting the val_n=24 seed42 mean above the iter-13 0.4616 read toward/past iter-5 0.508 -- and possibly nudging hr off 0. FALSIFIER: if SSIM stays in the 0.43-0.47 band the floor is the FBP bound itself (not optimization), FINALIZING the structural ceiling for the iter-20 writeup. hr expected ~0 either way (structurally FBP-bounded on dense 128-view phantoms). WALL: step budget UNCHANGED vs iter-13/14/15/16 (warm 12x200=2400 + per-image 24x600=14400 = 16800 steps); those ran 1400-1651 s. grad_clip changes neither step count nor per-step cost, so wall is identical, under the outer_wall_s=1700 guard and the 00:30:00 (1800 s) sbatch wall. All recon-affecting knobs IDENTICAL to the iter-13 seed42/val_n24 config (train_n=200, val_n=24, batch_size=1, seed=42, warm_start=True, pretrain_epochs=12, n_iter=600, lr=1e-4, unet_c=16, outer_wall_s=1700); ONLY grad_clip 1.0 -> 0.3 changed.

DIAGNOSIS (numbers, not pixels): the two val_n=24 seed reads landed seed42=0.4616 (iter-13, PSNR 13.45, hr 0.0011) and seed123=0.4431 (iter-14, PSNR 14.06, hr 0) -> |delta|=0.0185 -- TIGHTER than the val_n=12 seed42-vs-seed123 delta of 0.024 (iter-10 0.4724 vs iter-11 0.4484), confirming the iter-14 hypothesis that doubling 12->24 scenes shrinks the per-scan init stochasticity via the ~sqrt(2) averaging argument. BUT a 2-sample mean (0.4524) has an unconstrained standard error -- 'is ~0.45 the converged wider-basis ceiling?' is not finalizable from only two draws. This exactly mirrors the val_n=12 history, where a 3rd seed (seed=7, iter-12, 0.4305) was needed to turn the 2-sample pair into a 3-seed mean+/-std (0.4504, std 0.0173). FAILURE MODE = the 0.466 M-param U-Net OVERFITS each single noisy 128-view sparse-phantom scan (the 6-param bilateral twin physically cannot, which is why the twin clears baseline at hr+0.33 while this U-Net stays hr~0 at ~0.45-0.51 SSIM); the per-image fit has an init-driven stochastic noise floor that a wider val basis shrinks but does not eliminate. EXHAUSTED / FORBIDDEN axes (do NOT retry, per handoff): n_iter (iter-2 1200 steps 0.4785->0.4293, per-scan overfit), warm_start (iter-8 off -0.0595, load-bearing-positive), lr (iter-3 1e-3->1e-4 + iter-9 1e-4->2e-4 bracket 1e-4 as the per-scan optimum), pretrain_epochs (ep12 peak, ep18 worse 0.5016), unet_c (design-doc warned-against; mayo n2i c16->c32 flat 0.9508), grad_clip=1.0 (LOAD-BEARING 128/2304-view FBP-adjoint overflow guard, mandatory). The ONLY genuinely-untried confirmation knob is a 3RD seed AT the val_n=24 basis. LEVER CHOICE: seed 123 -> 7 at the val_n=24 PEAK config -- the SAME 3rd seed (7) used at val_n=12, so the val_n=24 3-seed mean is directly comparable to the val_n=12 3-seed mean (0.4504, std 0.0173), letting us read off how much the wider basis tightened the std. HYPOTHESIS: seed=7 at val_n=24 lands inside the [0.43, 0.47] band, yielding a 3-seed val_n=24 mean ~0.45 with a TIGHTER std than the val_n=12 0.0173 (the sqrt(2) averaging finally pinned down) -- a trustworthy, FINALIZED wider-basis ceiling for the per-image U-Net N2I on this synthetic 128-view substrate. hr stays ~0 (structurally FBP-bounded on dense 128-view phantoms). FALSIFIER: if seed=7 lands FAR outside [0.43, 0.47] (e.g. <0.41 or >0.49), the wider-basis std is NOT tighter than val_n=12 and the per-scan noise floor is INTRINSIC to the N2I objective (not just init-set sampling that wider averaging cancels) -- that wide intrinsic floor IS the documented ceiling finding, confirming the over-parameterized U-Net is the wrong tool here vs the bilateral twin (hr+0.33). Either branch FINALIZES the ceiling documentation toward the iter-20 mandate. WALL: warm 12x200=2400 + per-image 24x600=14400 = 16800 steps @ ~0.083 s/step ~= 1394 s; iter-13 ran this exact budget in 1651 s and iter-14 in 1533 s, under the outer_wall_s=1700 guard (per_scene_s = 1700/24 ~= 71 s, ample for 600 steps @ ~0.083 s/step ~= 50 s) and under the 00:30:00 (1800 s) sbatch wall. All recon-affecting knobs IDENTICAL to the iter-13/14 val_n=24 config (train_n=200, val_n=24, batch_size=1, grad_clip=1.0, warm_start=True, pretrain_epochs=12, n_iter=600, lr=1e-4, unet_c=16, outer_wall_s=1700); ONLY seed 123 -> 7 changed.

rationale: dual_domain_bilateral_n2i-claude-agentic: train_n=200, val_n=6, batch_size=1, grad_clip=1.0, seed=42, warm_start=True, pretrain_epochs=3, n_iter=400, outer_wall_s=1200, lr=0.0023, proj_n_bf=1, img_n_bf=7, proj_kernel=7, img_kernel=11, proj_sx=1.0, proj_sy=2.0, proj_sr=0.02, img_sx=5.5, img_sy=5.5, img_sr=0.02, rationale=iter-19: ONE knob changed vs the iter-18 WIN base (image-domain SPATIAL bilateral sigma img_sx/img_sy 4.5->5.5, BOTH x and y together = the isotropic image-domain spatial-extent sigma); all 18 other fields held IDENTICAL to demo_dl_dual_domain_bilateral_n2i_iter_18.json (img_kernel=11, img_n_bf=7, img_sr=0.02 LOOSE demo-correct, proj_n_bf=1, proj_kernel=7, proj_sx/sy=1.0/2.0, proj_sr=0.02, lr=2.3e-3, warm_start=True, pretrain_epochs=3, n_iter=400, train_n=200, val_n=6, grad_clip=1.0, seed=42 -> identical seed=42 val split, directly comparable to iter-18 SSIM 0.8401 / hr 0.3256 / PSNR 20.09). DECISIVE SATURATION TEST of the alternating sigma<->kernel ladder. Read iter-17->18 BY SSIM (the surface the spatial-smoothing thread moves; hr stays pinned ~0.325-0.333 at the 64-view-FBP noise-floor ceiling, an SSIM-only lever): iter-17 RE-LIBERATED sigma img_sx/img_sy 3.5->4.5 at kernel=9 -> SSIM 0.8284->0.8368 (+0.0084, ABOVE the 0.005 'meaningful' threshold); iter-18 widened kernel 9->11 -> SSIM 0.8368->0.8401 (+0.0033, BELOW the 0.005 threshold), hr flat 0.3251->0.3256, PSNR flat 20.08->20.09. The whole ladder trajectory: img_n_bf depth saturated SSIM/hr early; the image SPATIAL thread then climbed via alternating sigma<->kernel rungs -- SSIM 0.7796(iter6) ->0.7940(s2.5) ->0.8035(s3.5) ->0.8246(k7) ->0.8284(k9) ->0.8368(s4.5) ->0.8401(k11). The rung gains are decelerating: the sigma rungs gave +0.0144, +0.0095, +0.0084; the kernel rungs gave +0.0211, +0.0038, +0.0033. The LAST kernel rung (iter-18, +0.0033) fell BELOW the agent's own 0.005 meaningful-gain threshold -- the WINDOW lever is now exhausted. FAILURE-MODE / COUPLING DIAGNOSIS being tested: under the pre-registered ladder logic the next rung is the SIGMA (kernel just gave a sub-threshold step), but the coupling math warns this rung is near or past its substrate bound. A Gaussian of spatial sigma s needs ~+/-2s of support to be well-represented; at kernel=11 the window is +/-5px, while sigma=5.5 requests ~+/-11px (2*sigma) -- so sigma=5.5 is AGAIN window-truncated (half-window 5 < sigma 5.5), the same over-request regime that flattened iter-14. So this rung tests EXACTLY whether ANY residual sigma headroom remains inside the kernel=11 window: at kernel=9 the sigma re-lib 3.5->4.5 still paid +0.0084 because the window (then +/-4) had just been widened ahead of the sigma; here the window is only +/-5px for a requested +/-11px Gaussian, so the marginal extra averaging the window can actually deliver is small. HYPOTHESIS (img-spatial-4, ceiling-doc): widening img_sx/img_sy 4.5->5.5 at kernel=11 yields a SUB-THRESHOLD SSIM gain (<0.005) or regresses, while hr stays pinned ~0.325-0.333 and PSNR flat ~20.1 -- CONFIRMING the image-domain spatial-denoising ladder has reached the ~0.84 SSIM / ~0.33 hr substrate bound: the 6-param bilateral cannot extract more than the 64-view (half of 128) FBP noise floor allows on this synthetic phantom substrate. If instead SSIM rises meaningfully (>0.005), the sigma still has headroom even inside the +/-5px window and iter-20 would widen the kernel one final notch (11->13) to confirm the ladder is genuinely climbing rather than at its bound -- either way iter-19 cleanly resolves box-(4): does the climb continue past 0.8401 or has image-domain spatial denoising hit the ~0.84 SSIM substrate bound? Chose img_sx/img_sy 4.5->5.5 (the pre-registered ladder continuation -- the SIGMA rung, since the kernel just delivered a sub-threshold +0.0033) over (a) pushing img_kernel 11->13 NOW (the kernel rung just fell below the 0.005 threshold at iter-18 -- the window is no longer the binding lever, and widening it further with the unchanged sigma=4.5 it already mostly contains is the lowest-EV move), (b) proj_sr/proj_kernel/proj_n_bf (whole proj domain confirmed flat at iter-11/12 -- symmetry trap, wasted), (c) img_sr (exhausted + substrate-confirmed WRONG-direction -- tightening to 0.0005 collapsed hr 0.3335->0.1998 at iter-4 -- FORBIDDEN, stays LOOSE 0.02), (d) img_n_bf/n_iter/pretrain_epochs/seed/val_n (all DEAD FLAT / variance-only, exhausted), (e) grad_clip (mandatory overflow guard at 1.0, not a quality lever). Held fixed at iter-18 values: img_kernel=11, img_n_bf=7, img_sr=0.02 (LOOSE, demo-correct), proj_n_bf=1, proj_kernel=7, proj_sr=0.02, proj_sx=1.0/proj_sy=2.0, lr=2.3e-3, warm_start=True, pretrain_epochs=3, n_iter=400, train_n=200, val_n=6, grad_clip=1.0, seed=42. Wall: iter-18 ran 1045 s at img_kernel=11; img_sx/img_sy are pure init sigma values inside the fixed img_kernel=11 window -> ZERO added compute, wall ~unchanged, comfortably under the 1800 s sbatch wall and the 1200 s outer_wall_s internal guard (under the 15-min budget). PER-IMAGE bilateral N2I, AGENT4CT_DATASET=phantoms; warm_start STAYS ON; do NOT revert to amortized; do NOT tighten img_sr.

rationale: dual_domain_bilateral_n2i-claude-agentic: train_n=200, val_n=6, batch_size=1, grad_clip=1.0, seed=42, warm_start=True, pretrain_epochs=3, n_iter=400, outer_wall_s=1200, lr=0.0023, proj_n_bf=1, img_n_bf=7, proj_kernel=7, img_kernel=11, proj_sx=1.0, proj_sy=2.0, proj_sr=0.02, img_sx=4.5, img_sy=4.5, img_sr=0.02, rationale=iter-18: ONE knob changed vs the iter-17 WIN base (image-domain bilateral WINDOW SIZE img_kernel 9->11); all 18 other fields held IDENTICAL to demo_dl_dual_domain_bilateral_n2i_iter_17.json (img_sx/img_sy=4.5, img_n_bf=7, img_sr=0.02 LOOSE demo-correct, proj_n_bf=1, proj_kernel=7, proj_sx/sy=1.0/2.0, proj_sr=0.02, lr=2.3e-3, warm_start=True, pretrain_epochs=3, n_iter=400, train_n=200, val_n=6, grad_clip=1.0, seed=42 -> identical seed=42 val split, directly comparable to iter-17 SSIM 0.8368 / hr 0.3251 / PSNR 20.08). THE PRE-REGISTERED iter-18 STEP: WIDEN THE WINDOW that the re-liberated sigma now requests. Read iter-16->17 BY SSIM (the surface the spatial-smoothing thread moves; hr stays pinned ~0.325-0.332 at the 64-view-FBP noise-floor ceiling, an SSIM-only lever): iter-16 img_kernel 7->9 gave SSIM 0.8246->0.8284 (+0.0038, kernel thread saturating at the then-sigma=3.5); iter-17 RE-LIBERATED the sigma img_sx/img_sy 3.5->4.5 at kernel=9 and LIFTED SSIM 0.8284->0.8368 (+0.0084, STILL CLIMBING -- bigger than the saturating iter-16 kernel step), while hr stayed pinned (0.3283->0.3251) and PSNR flat (20.12->20.08). So sigma re-liberation is the live thread and it is NOT yet saturated. SIGMA/KERNEL COUPLING READ (the binding constraint flipped back to the WINDOW): a Gaussian of spatial sigma s needs ~+/-2s of support to be well-represented; at img_sx=4.5 that is ~+/-9px requested, but img_kernel=9 gives only a +/-4px window (half-window 4 < sigma 4.5). So the sigma=4.5 Gaussian is AGAIN truncated by the window -- the +0.0084 lift at iter-17 was the sigma reaching the +/-4px window edge, and the WINDOW is once more the binding constraint (2*sigma~9px > 4px half-window). FAILURE MODE this iter addresses: at kernel=9 the img_sx=4.5 spatial weight is clipped at the +/-4px window edge -- the BF cannot average over the full ~+/-5px (kernel=11) / ~+/-9px (2*sigma) neighborhood the sigma=4.5 requests. The unlock is to widen the WINDOW, not push the sigma further (pushing sigma 4.5->5.5 now would request even MORE support from a window that already truncates it -- the exact iter-14 saturation regime). This is the alternating sigma<->kernel ladder explicitly pre-registered in iter-17's rationale: 'If SSIM rises meaningfully, the sigma still has headroom and the alternating sigma<->kernel ladder continues (iter-18 would widen kernel 9->11)'. SSIM rose +0.0084 (meaningfully), so the ladder continues to the kernel. HYPOTHESIS (img-kernel-3): widening img_kernel 9->11 enlarges each per-BF window from +/-4px to +/-5px so the img_sx=4.5 spatial Gaussian can average over (more of) the neighborhood it requests -> lifts SSIM past iter-17 0.8368 on the SAME seed=42 split. Expect hr to stay pinned ~0.325-0.332 (this whole spatial thread is an SSIM-only structural-similarity lever bounded by the 64-view-FBP noise floor -- hr flat across iter-13..17). DIAGNOSTIC: if SSIM rises meaningfully (gain >0.005) the climb continues and iter-19 would RE-LIBERATE the sigma again (4.5->5.5 now that kernel=11 admits it) -- the ladder is not yet at its substrate bound; if SSIM SATURATES or regresses (gain <0.005) the image-domain spatial denoising is exhausted at the ~0.84 SSIM / ~0.33 hr substrate bound -- the 6-param bilateral cannot extract more than the 64-view (half of 128) FBP noise floor allows on this synthetic phantom substrate -- a clean ceiling-doc result toward iter-20. Chose img_kernel 9->11 (the EXPLICITLY pre-registered iter-18 next step -- continue the alternating ladder by raising the binding constraint, which is now the WINDOW since 2*sigma=9px > the kernel=9 +/-4px half-window) over (a) pushing img_sx/img_sy 4.5->5.5 NOW (the sigma is window-truncated at kernel=9, so widening it further requests support the +/-4px window cannot deliver -- the iter-14 saturation regime; widen the window FIRST, re-liberate sigma at iter-19 if the kernel saturates), (b) proj_sr/proj_kernel/proj_n_bf (whole proj domain confirmed flat at iter-11/12 -- symmetry trap, wasted), (c) img_sr (exhausted + substrate-confirmed WRONG-direction -- tightening to 0.0005 collapsed hr 0.3335->0.1998 at iter-4 -- FORBIDDEN, stays LOOSE 0.02), (d) img_n_bf/n_iter/pretrain_epochs/seed/val_n (all DEAD FLAT / variance-only, exhausted), (e) grad_clip (mandatory overflow guard at 1.0, not a quality lever). Held fixed at iter-17 values: img_sx=4.5/img_sy=4.5, img_n_bf=7, img_sr=0.02 (LOOSE, demo-correct), proj_n_bf=1, proj_kernel=7, proj_sr=0.02, proj_sx=1.0/proj_sy=2.0, lr=2.3e-3, warm_start=True, pretrain_epochs=3, n_iter=400, train_n=200, val_n=6, grad_clip=1.0, seed=42. Wall: iter-16/17 ran ~762-764 s at img_kernel=9; an 11-px image-BF window is modestly slower per step than a 9-px window (the image-domain conv is a small fraction of the 128-view FBP+proj per-step cost) -- n_iter=400/val_n=6 kept at iter-17 values, so wall stays comfortably under the 1800 s sbatch wall and the 1200 s outer_wall_s internal guard (under the 15-min budget). PER-IMAGE bilateral N2I, AGENT4CT_DATASET=phantoms; warm_start STAYS ON; do NOT revert to amortized; do NOT tighten img_sr.

The ceiling estimate's BASIS is still only 12 scenes per read; whether the ~0.47 seed42 mean is representative of a wider scene set is the one remaining un-pinned-down quantity in the ceiling documentation. FAILURE MODE = the 0.466 M-param U-Net OVERFITS each single noisy 128-view sparse-phantom scan (the 6-param bilateral twin physically cannot, which is why the twin clears baseline at hr+0.33 while this U-Net stays hr~0 at ~0.45-0.51 SSIM); the per-image fit has an init-driven stochastic noise floor that a wider val basis shrinks but does not eliminate. LEVER CHOICE (the genuinely-untried confirmation knob, exactly the handoff's named candidate): val_n 12 -> 24 at the seed42 PEAK config. WALL: warm 12x200=2400 + per-image 24x600=14400 = 16800 steps @ ~0.083 s/step ~= 1394 s, under the raised outer_wall_s=1700 guard (per_scene_s = 1700/24 ~= 71 s, ample for 600 steps @ ~0.083 s/step ~= 50 s) and under the 00:30:00 (1800 s) sbatch wall. PUSH THE SAME WINNING LEVER FURTHER. Read iter-13 BY SSIM/HEADROOM (campaign primary; SSIM is the surface the spatial lever moved): iter-13 widened img_sx/img_sy 1.5->2.5 and LIFTED SSIM 0.7796->0.7940 (+0.0144, the run best), while hr stayed FLAT at 0.3332 (~iter-6 0.3330) -- the image-domain SPATIAL sigma is the FIRST lever in the whole run to break the SSIM plateau (img_n_bf depth had saturated SSIM growth and hr; proj domain fully inert at iter-11/12). FAILURE MODE iter-13 addressed and this iter re-probes: the 7-deep image bilateral cascade was UNDER-SMOOTHING the broad post-FBP noise floor at the default spatial sigma 1.5 -- widening the spatial neighborhood (sigma 1.5->2.5) let each of the 7 image BFs average over a larger support and smooth that broad noise floor, lifting the structural-similarity term while the LOOSE img_sr=0.02 kept it edge-preserving (no blur across phantom edges). KEY DIAGNOSTIC / RISK: img_kernel is held at 5, so the discrete bilateral WINDOW is +/-2 px. At sigma 2.5 the Gaussian spatial weight is already near-flat across that 5-px window (iter-13 noted 2.5 is near the window edge); at sigma 3.5 the spatial weight is even FLATTER -> the kernel=5 window, not the sigma, may now be the binding constraint, in which case SSIM saturates (or moves only marginally) because the BF can't actually reach the wider support the sigma requests. If SSIM SATURATES or regresses here, that pinpoints img_kernel (window SIZE) as the iter-15 lever -- widen img_kernel 5->7/9 to let the larger spatial sigma act over a genuinely larger window (the pre-registered next step from iter-13's rationale: 'img_kernel is the iter-14 candidate if img_sx/sy moves hr' -- img_sx/sy DID move SSIM, so kernel is now the live follow-on once sigma saturates). If SSIM KEEPS rising, the spatial sigma still has headroom inside the kernel=5 window and iter-15 pushes sigma further (4.5) before touching the kernel. Chose img_sx/img_sy 2.5->3.5 (the SAME winning lever, one notch further -- the steer's explicit instruction) over (a) img_kernel (the natural follow-on, but only AFTER confirming whether sigma alone saturates inside the current window -- changing kernel now would confound the sigma-saturation question), (b) proj_sr/proj_kernel/proj_n_bf (whole proj domain confirmed flat at iter-11/12 -- symmetry trap, wasted), (c) img_sr (exhausted + substrate-confirmed WRONG-direction -- tightening collapsed hr 0.3335->0.1998 at iter-4 -- FORBIDDEN, do NOT tighten; stays LOOSE 0.02), (d) img_n_bf/n_iter/pretrain_epochs/seed/val_n (all DEAD FLAT / variance-only, exhausted), (e) grad_clip (mandatory overflow guard at 1.0, not a quality lever). Held fixed at iter-13 values: img_n_bf=7, img_sr=0.02 (LOOSE, demo-correct), proj_n_bf=1, proj_kernel=7, proj_sr=0.02, img_kernel=5, proj_sx=1.0/proj_sy=2.0, lr=2.3e-3, warm_start=True, pretrain_epochs=3, n_iter=400, train_n=200, val_n=6, grad_clip=1.0, seed=42. Wall: iter-13 ran well under budget; img_sx/img_sy are pure init sigma values inside the fixed img_kernel=5 window -> ZERO added compute, wall ~unchanged, comfortably under the 1800 s sbatch wall and the 1200 s outer_wall_s internal guard (under the 15-min budget). PER-IMAGE bilateral N2I, AGENT4CT_DATASET=phantoms; warm_start STAYS ON; do NOT revert to amortized; do NOT tighten img_sr.

Read iter-11->12 BY HEADROOM (campaign primary, PSNR/noise-sensitive on demo): iter-11 proj_sr 0.02->0.05 (LOOSEN proj RANGE) DEAD FLAT (hr 0.3330->0.33285, PSNR 20.18->20.181, SSIM 0.7796->0.7790); iter-12 proj_kernel 7->9 (proj SPATIAL extent) DEAD FLAT (hr 0.3330->0.33296, PSNR 20.18->20.1825, SSIM 0.7796->0.7796). FAILURE MODE being documented: hr~0.42 (seed-123 regime) / hr~0.333 (seed-42 regime) is the 6-param bilateral's structural noise-floor ceiling on the 64-view (half of 128) FBP -- it is IMAGE-DOMAIN-FBP-BOUNDED on this 128-view phantom substrate. EVERY image-domain CAPACITY/ANCHOR lever is exhausted: image-domain DEPTH (img_n_bf, hr slope collapsed to ~0 by n_bf=5: 1->3 +0.051, 3->5 +0.006, 5->7 +0.000), per-scan OPTIMIZER budget (n_iter flat 400->800; the 6-param BF physically CANNOT overfit one scan), warm-start anchor length (pretrain_epochs flat 3->6), seed (8->confirmed split-variance only), val_n (9->confirmed hr~0.41 real on seed-123). img_sr is EXHAUSTED + substrate-confirmed WRONG-direction (demo wants LOOSE 0.02; tightening to 0.0005 collapsed hr 0.3335->0.1998 at iter-4 -- FORBIDDEN, do NOT tighten). The ONE genuinely-untried knob remaining in the LOOSE-img_sr regime is the image-domain SPATIAL sigma img_sx/img_sy -- pinned at 1.5/1.5 across ALL 12 prior iters, NEVER varied. img_sr (range) governs how much the image BF acts ACROSS intensity jumps (edge selectivity); img_sx/img_sy (spatial) govern the SPATIAL neighborhood over which it averages WITHIN an edge-bounded region -- a DISTINCT, orthogonal axis to range AND to depth. HYPOTHESIS (img-spatial): widening img_sx/img_sy 1.5->2.5 enlarges the image-domain averaging neighborhood, giving each of the 7 image BFs a larger spatial support to smooth the broad post-FBP noise floor (the demo-relevant axis since hr here is PSNR/noise-sensitive) while staying edge-preserving via the unchanged LOOSE img_sr=0.02 -> may lift hr/PSNR above iter-6 ~0.333 / PSNR 20.18 on the SAME seed=42 split. Direction is WIDER (more smoothing of the noise floor), which is the demo-correct over-smoothing axis (demo wants MORE noise smoothing -- the whole img_n_bf depth arc earned hr by adding noise-smoothing capacity); the unchanged LOOSE img_sr keeps it from blurring across phantom edges. If hr/PSNR stay FLAT, it CLOSES the image-domain spatial-extent ceiling question: the 6-param bilateral is structurally inert on its spatial sigma too, confirming the ~hr 0.33 ceiling is the 64-view-FBP noise floor regardless of spatial support -- a clean ceiling-doc result toward iter-20. Chose img_sx/img_sy (image SPATIAL, the last untouched image-domain axis named in the steer) over (a) proj_sr/proj_kernel/proj_n_bf (whole proj domain just confirmed flat at iter-11/12 -- symmetry trap, wasted), (b) img_sr (exhausted + WRONG-direction, FORBIDDEN), (c) img_n_bf/n_iter/pretrain_epochs/seed/val_n (all DEAD FLAT / variance-only, exhausted), (d) img_kernel (also untouched at 5, but img_kernel sets the discrete window SIZE while img_sx/sy set the continuous spatial sigma WITHIN that window -- sigma is the finer, more-informed lever and at kernel=5 a sigma of 2.5 is near the window edge, so vary sigma first; img_kernel is the iter-14 candidate if img_sx/sy moves hr), (e) grad_clip (mandatory 2304-view-adjoint overflow guard at 1.0 -- a stability guard, not a quality lever). Held fixed at iter-6 PEAK values: img_n_bf=7, img_sr=0.02 (LOOSE, demo-correct), proj_n_bf=1, proj_kernel=7, proj_sr=0.02, img_kernel=5, proj_sx=1.0/proj_sy=2.0, lr=2.3e-3, warm_start=True, pretrain_epochs=3, n_iter=400, train_n=200, val_n=6, grad_clip=1.0, seed=42. Wall: iter-6 ran 828 s, iter-11 ran 330 s, iter-12 similar; img_sx/img_sy are pure init sigma values inside the fixed img_kernel=5 window -> ZERO added compute, wall ~unchanged, comfortably under the 1800 s sbatch wall and the 1200 s outer_wall_s internal guard (under the 15-min budget). PER-IMAGE bilateral N2I, AGENT4CT_DATASET=phantoms; warm_start STAYS ON; do NOT revert to amortized; do NOT tighten img_sr.

rationale: dual_domain_bilateral_n2i-claude-agentic: train_n=200, val_n=6, batch_size=1, grad_clip=1.0, seed=42, warm_start=True, pretrain_epochs=3, n_iter=400, outer_wall_s=1200, lr=0.0023, proj_n_bf=1, img_n_bf=7, proj_kernel=9, img_kernel=5, proj_sx=1.0, proj_sy=2.0, proj_sr=0.02, img_sx=1.5, img_sy=1.5, img_sr=0.02, rationale=iter-12: ONE knob changed vs the iter-6 hr-0.4222 PEAK base (proj_kernel 7->9, the PROJECTION-domain bilateral SPATIAL kernel size); all 18 other fields held IDENTICAL to demo_dl_dual_domain_bilateral_n2i_iter_06.json (img_n_bf=7, img_sr=0.02 LOOSE demo-correct, proj_n_bf=1, img_k=5, proj_sx/sy=1.0/2.0, proj_sr=0.02, img_sx/sy=1.5/1.5, lr=2.3e-3, warm_start=True, pretrain_epochs=3, n_iter=400, train_n=200, val_n=6, grad_clip=1.0, seed=42 -> identical seed=42 val split, directly comparable to iter-6 hr 0.3330 / PSNR 20.18 / SSIM 0.7796). BASED ON iter-6 (NOT iter-11): iter-11 proj_sr 0.02->0.05 (LOOSEN proj RANGE sigma) was DEAD FLAT -- hr 0.3330->0.33285 (-0.00015), PSNR 20.18->20.181 (identical to 3 dp), SSIM 0.7796->0.7790. So loosening the proj RANGE did NOT help; the proj-range axis is in the symmetry trap (do NOT push proj_sr further, do NOT stack proj_n_bf -- both wasted-param moves on the near-identity proj filter). Per the steer, since proj_sr was flat I base on the iter-6 hr-peak config, not the iter-11 config. FAILURE MODE at hr~0.42 (seed-123 regime) / hr~0.333 (seed-42 regime): the 6-param bilateral sits at its structural noise-floor ceiling on the 64-view (half of 128) FBP; EVERY image-side lever (img_n_bf depth saturated, n_iter flat, pretrain_epochs flat) and the proj RANGE sigma (iter-11 flat) are exhausted, and img_sr tightening is substrate-confirmed WRONG-direction (collapsed hr 0.3335->0.1998 at iter-4 -- forbidden). The ONE proj-domain axis NEVER probed at the peak is the proj SPATIAL kernel SIZE (proj_kernel). proj_sr (range) governs how much the proj BF acts across intensity jumps; proj_kernel (spatial extent) governs the neighborhood over which it averages -- a DISTINCT, orthogonal lever. The iter-11 flat-range result tested only the range axis, not the spatial-extent axis. HYPOTHESIS (proj-spatial): widening proj_kernel 7->9 enlarges the sinogram-domain averaging neighborhood, giving the single proj BF a larger spatial support to smooth correlated 64-view sinogram streak-noise BEFORE the FBP adjoint -- a denoising axis orthogonal to both the exhausted image-domain levers AND the inert proj range sigma -> may lift hr/PSNR above iter-6 ~0.333 / PSNR 20.18 on the SAME seed=42 split. If hr/PSNR stay FLAT, it CLOSES the proj-domain ceiling question: the proj stack is structurally inert on this 128-view phantom substrate on BOTH its axes (range AND spatial extent), confirming the ~hr 0.33 ceiling is image-domain-FBP-bounded -- a clean ceiling-doc result toward iter-20. Chose proj_kernel (spatial) over (a) proj_sr-further / proj_n_bf (symmetry trap -- range axis just confirmed flat at iter-11, stacking is wasted), (b) grad_clip (mandatory 2304-view-adjoint overflow guard at 1.0 -- a stability guard, not a quality lever; perturbing it risks instability with no quality-improvement story), (c) img_sr (exhausted + WRONG-direction -- forbidden), (d) img_n_bf/n_iter/pretrain_epochs (all DEAD FLAT, exhausted). proj_kernel is the last UNTOUCHED proj-domain axis and the prompt's named candidate set. Held fixed at iter-6 PEAK values: img_n_bf=7, img_sr=0.02 (LOOSE, demo-correct), proj_n_bf=1, proj_sr=0.02, img_kernel=5, proj_sx=1.0/proj_sy=2.0, img_sx=1.5/img_sy=1.5, lr=2.3e-3, warm_start=True, pretrain_epochs=3, n_iter=400, train_n=200, val_n=6, grad_clip=1.0, seed=42. Wall: iter-6 ran 828 s, iter-11 ran 330 s; a slightly larger proj kernel (7->9) adds a small per-step sinogram-conv cost only, comfortably under the 1800 s sbatch wall and the 1200 s outer_wall_s internal guard (under the 15-min budget). PER-IMAGE bilateral N2I, AGENT4CT_DATASET=phantoms; warm_start STAYS ON; do NOT revert to amortized; do NOT tighten img_sr.

rationale: dual_domain_n2i-claude-agentic: train_n=200, val_n=12, batch_size=1, grad_clip=1.0, seed=42, warm_start=True, pretrain_epochs=12, n_iter=600, outer_wall_s=1200, lr=0.0001, unet_c=16, rationale=iter-10: ONE knob -> val_n 6 -> 12 (2x val scenes) at the iter-5 PEAK base (seed42/ep12/lr1e-4/warm_start True/n_iter600/grad_clip1.0, SSIM 0.5081). NOT the iter-9 lr2e-4 (dead: 0.4697 confirms 1e-4 optimal), NOT iter-8 warm_start=off (dead: 0.4486), NOT the iter-7 seed123 basin. lr RESET 2e-4 -> 1e-4 (the per-scan overfit-anchor optimum). DIAGNOSIS (numbers, not pixels): iter-8 warm_start OFF dropped 0.5081->0.4486 (-0.0595, load-bearing-positive, settled); iter-9 lr 1e-4->2e-4 dropped 0.5081->0.4697 (-0.0384 vs the ep12 peak), so 1e-4 is confirmed the per-scan step optimum at the converged init. BOTH iter-8 and iter-9 came back NEGATIVE, closing warm_start and lr as levers. FAILURE MODE = the 0.466 M-param U-Net OVERFITS each single noisy 128-view sparse-phantom scan (the 6-param bilateral twin physically cannot, which is why the twin clears baseline at hr+0.33 while this U-Net stays hr0 at ~0.51 SSIM); AND the per-image fit has a LARGE init-driven STOCHASTIC NOISE FLOOR -- a seed flip 42->123 alone swung SSIM 0.5081->0.4203 (-0.088) at the SAME ep12/lr1e-4 config (iter-5 vs iter-7). That noise floor is the real obstacle to *documenting* the ceiling: every single-val read is contaminated by per-scan stochasticity, so 'is 0.51 the converged ceiling or just one lucky/unlucky draw?' is unanswerable at val_n=6. EXHAUSTED axes (do NOT retry): n_iter (iter-2 1200 steps 0.4785->0.4293, U-Net overfits one scan), warm_start (iter-8 off -0.06), lr (iter-3 1e-3->1e-4 + iter-9 1e-4->2e-4 both bracket 1e-4 as optimal), pretrain_epochs (ep12 peak, ep18 worse 0.5016), unet_c (mayo n2i c16->c32 flat 0.9508, design-doc warned-against). grad_clip=1.0 is LOAD-BEARING (the 2304/128-view FBP-adjoint overflow guard, mandatory -- do NOT touch). LEVER CHOICE (the one genuinely-untried knob with real value -- box-3 candidate): val_n 6 -> 12, a CLEANER NOISE-FLOOR READ. Doubling the number of val scenes averages the per-scan SSIM over 2x as many independent draws, shrinking the standard error of the ceiling estimate by ~sqrt(2) and directly attacking the documented stochastic-noise-floor obstacle. This is a CEILING-DOCUMENTATION move (toward the iter-20 mandate of *documenting* why this ceiling holds), not a ceiling-raising move: I do NOT expect hr to move off ~0 (structurally FBP-bounded on dense 128-view phantoms). HYPOTHESIS: at val_n=12 the mean SSIM lands near ~0.50-0.51 (the ep12/lr1e-4 peak family) with a TIGHTER read than the noisy val_n=6 single-seed numbers, giving a more-trustworthy ~0.51 ceiling estimate for the U-Net N2I on this synthetic 128-view substrate. FALSIFIER: if the val_n=12 mean lands FAR from 0.51 (e.g. <0.46 or >0.55), the val_n=6 set was itself unrepresentative and the ceiling claim needs the wider val set as its basis going forward. NOTE: val_n changes the absolute SSIM's comparability to iters 1-9 (different/larger scene set) -- that is the POINT (a cleaner, less-noisy basis), and it is recorded here so future iters read val_n=12 numbers against THIS iter, not the val_n=6 history. WALL: warm 12x200=2400 (unchanged) + per-image 12x600=7200 = 9600 steps @ ~0.083 s/step ~= 800 s, under the outer_wall_s=1200 guard and the 00:30:00 (1800 s) sbatch wall (per_scene_s = 1200/12 = 100 s each, ample for 600 steps @ ~0.083 s/step ~= 50 s). All other knobs IDENTICAL to the iter-5 PEAK config (train_n=200, batch_size=1, grad_clip=1.0, seed=42, warm_start=True, pretrain_epochs=12, n_iter=600, lr=1e-4, unet_c=16); ONLY val_n 6 -> 12 changed.

FAILURE MODE = the 0.466 M-param U-Net OVERFITS each single noisy 128-view sparse-phantom scan (the 6-param bilateral twin physically cannot, which is why the twin clears baseline at hr+0.33 while this U-Net stays hr0 at ~0.51 SSIM); AND the per-image fit has a LARGE init-driven STOCHASTIC NOISE FLOOR -- a seed flip 42->123 alone swung SSIM 0.5081->0.4203 (-0.088) at the SAME ep12/lr1e-4 config (iter-5 vs iter-7). KEEP warm_start=True (LOAD-BEARING-POSITIVE, settled), pretrain_epochs=12 (the init-budget PEAK), seed=42 (the good basin), grad_clip=1.0 (LOAD-BEARING 128-view FBP-adjoint guard, mandatory -- do NOT touch), n_iter=600, val_n=6 (UNCHANGED so SSIM stays iter-to-iter comparable). DIAGNOSIS (numbers, not pixels): the load-bearing-positive warm_start fact is now re-confirmed on demo -- iter-8 warm_start OFF (seed42/ep12) dropped SSIM 0.5081 -> 0.4486 (-0.0595, hr0, PSNR 16.38->16.29), so without the amortized pre-pass each per-scan lr-anchored fit lands in a worse basin. FAILURE MODE = per-image U-Net N2I caps ~0.51 SSIM (hr~0) on this 128-view synthetic-phantom substrate: it is FBP-bounded AND has a large init-driven stochastic noise floor (a seed flip 42->123 alone swung 0.5081->0.4203, -0.088, iter-5 vs iter-7), so single-seed reads are intrinsically noisy here and the U-Net (0.466 M params) overfits one noisy scan where the 6-param bilateral twin physically cannot (twin clears baseline at hr+0.33). LEVER CHOICE: of the genuinely-untried-at-PEAK knobs (pretrain_epochs is EXHAUSTED -- ep12 peak, ep18 worse; grad_clip is LOAD-BEARING/forbidden; val_n change would break iter-to-iter SSIM comparability), do the mild lr RE-CONFIRM the handoff lists: 1e-4 -> 2e-4. lr=1e-4 was picked at iter-3 as the per-scan OVERFIT ANCHOR (1e-3 -> 1e-4 lifted 0.4785 -> 0.4880 by keeping Adam pinned near the warm-start init), but 1e-4 vs 2e-4 was never compared at the converged ep12 PEAK -- only 1e-3 vs 1e-4 at the under-trained ep3 init. So whether 1e-4 is the true per-scan step optimum AT THE PEAK init is untested. HYPOTHESIS: at the ep12/seed42 peak init, a 2x larger per-scan step (2e-4) lets the lr-anchored fit refine slightly further off a now-good warm-start init without descending into the single-scan noise-fitting minimum that killed n_iter (iter-2 1200 steps regressed). If SSIM rises >0.51 then 1e-4 was slightly under-stepping at the converged init (the anchor optimum shifts up once the init is good); if it falls toward ~0.48-0.49 then 1e-4 is confirmed optimal (2e-4 starts to overfit the single scan) and the per-scan anchor axis is settled. rationale: dual_domain_n2i-claude-agentic: train_n=200, val_n=6, batch_size=1, grad_clip=1.0, seed=42, warm_start=False, pretrain_epochs=12, n_iter=600, outer_wall_s=1200, lr=0.0001, unet_c=16, rationale=iter-8: ONE knob -> warm_start true -> false (per-image fit starts from a FIXED fresh U-Net init, NO amortized GT-free pre-pass). Seed RESET 123 -> 42 (the baseline seed of iters 1-6) so the warm_start ON/OFF contrast is clean against the ep12/seed42 PEAK (0.5081), not confounded by the seed-123 basin. KEEP lr=1e-4 (per-scan overfit anchor, iter-3 winner), pretrain_epochs=12 (the peak init budget -- inert when warm_start=False but left at peak for a clean toggle-back if needed). DIAGNOSIS (numbers, not pixels): the iter-7 seed probe's FALSIFIER FIRED. Trend ep12/lr1e-4: seed42 SSIM 0.5081 PSNR 16.376 (iter-5 PEAK); seed42/ep18 0.5016 PSNR 16.29 (iter-6); seed123/ep12 0.4203 PSNR 13.085 (iter-7). Flipping ONLY the seed dropped SSIM 0.5081 -> 0.4203 (-0.088) and PSNR 16.38 -> 13.09 dB (-3.3 dB) -- far outside the iter-7 falsifier band (predicted +/-0.01, threshold <0.49). So ~0.51 is NOT a cleanly-converged structural ceiling; the per-image fit has a LARGE stochastic noise floor. FAILURE MODE = the per-scan U-Net N2I operating point is FRAGILE to initialization: the amortized warm-start pre-pass lands in variable basins (seed42 good, seed123 bad), and the lr=1e-4 per-scan fit is anchored to whatever basin it inherits, so init variance -> output variance. n_iter is RULED OUT (iter-2 1200 steps REGRESSED 0.4785->0.4293), pretrain_epochs is EXHAUSTED/turned-over (ep12 peak, ep18 worse), unet_c is the explicitly-warned-against axis, grad_clip=1.0 is LOAD-BEARING (128-view FBP adjoint guard, mandatory -- do NOT touch). LEVER CHOICE (the one untried per-image knob with real headroom): warm_start ON->OFF. This directly tests whether the amortized init is HELPING or is the SOURCE of the seed-fragility: with warm_start=False the per-scan fit starts from a deterministic fresh U-Net (no pre-pass basin lottery), isolating the per-scan N2I objective's own variance. WARM-START-FRAGILITY HYPOTHESIS: the 0.5081->0.4203 seed swing is driven by the warm-start pre-pass landing in variable basins. (a) If warm_start=False SSIM stabilizes near/above ~0.48 with much smaller seed sensitivity, the warm-start was net-fragility (possibly near-neutral on mean) and the per-scan fit alone is the real, more-robust operating point -- a cleaner basis to then re-probe. (b) If SSIM COLLAPSES well below 0.42, the warm-start init was load-bearing POSITIVE and the seed swing is intrinsic to the per-scan N2I objective on this 128-view synthetic substrate -- which CONFIRMS (with the bilateral twin's hr+0.33 at 6 params that physically cannot overfit) that an over-parameterized U-Net is the wrong tool here, documenting the structural ceiling for iter-20. Either branch is informative toward the iter-20 mandate. hr expected ~0 (structurally FBP-bounded on dense-view phantoms). WALL: warm_start=False ELIMINATES the 12x200=2400-step pre-pass, leaving ONLY per-image 6x600=3600 steps @ ~0.083 s/step ~= 300 s (iter-7 was 544 s WITH the pre-pass), comfortably under the 15-min target, the outer_wall_s=1200 guard, and the 00:30:00 (1800 s) sbatch wall -- no need to drop val_n/n_iter. All other knobs IDENTICAL to the iter-5 PEAK config (train_n=200, val_n=6, batch_size=1, grad_clip=1.0, pretrain_epochs=12, n_iter=600, lr=1e-4, unet_c=16); ONLY warm_start true->false (and seed reset 123->42 to anchor the ON/OFF comparison).

DIAGNOSIS (numbers, not pixels): the init lever (warm-start pretrain_epochs) climbed then SATURATED AND TURNED OVER -- iter-3 ep3 0.4880; iter-4 ep6 0.4957 (+0.0077); iter-5 ep12 0.5081 (+0.0124, PSNR 16.376, the PEAK); iter-6 ep18 0.5016 (-0.0065, PSNR 16.29 -- DID NOT beat ep12). The iter-5/iter-6 falsifier FIRED: more init budget past ep12 no longer helps (over-converges the amortized warm-start pre-pass / the per-scan lr=1e-4 fit cannot exploit a noisier init), so the init axis is EXHAUSTED. n_iter is RULED OUT (iter-2 1200 steps REGRESSED 0.4785->0.4293, per-scan U-Net overfits one noisy scan) and unet_c is the explicitly-warned-against axis (solver design doc: capacity is NOT the lever for this loss; mayo n2i c16->c32 flat 0.9508). FAILURE MODE = per-image U-Net N2I has converged to its structural ceiling (~0.51 SSIM, hr~0) on this 128-view synthetic-phantom substrate; the 0.5081<->0.5016 swing between the two best inits is within noise, not a real lever. LEVER CHOICE (a NOT-yet-tried axis): of seed / grad_clip / unet_c-retest, pick SEED. seed=42 was FIXED across all 6 prior iters, so the per-image noise floor is unmeasured; flipping seed 42->123 at the PEAK config (ep12, lr1e-4, n_iter600) re-randomizes the warm-start init + the angular-subset split + Adam init, giving a clean read of how much of the 0.5081<->0.5016 swing is stochastic. grad_clip=1.0 is LOAD-BEARING (the 128-view FBP adjoint guard -- mandatory per campaign-state, do NOT touch) and unet_c is warned-against, so seed is the safest, most-informative ceiling-doc probe. HYPOTHESIS: at seed=123/ep12/lr1e-4 the SSIM lands within ~+/-0.01 of the 0.5081 ep12 peak (i.e. inside the 0.5016<->0.5081 band), confirming ~0.51 is the per-image U-Net N2I ceiling on demo and that the ep18 dip was noise, not a real init turn-over. hr stays 0 (structurally FBP-bounded on dense-view phantoms -- the U-Net overfits one scan where the bilateral twin's 6 params cannot, which is why the twin clears baseline at hr+0.33). rationale: dual_domain_bilateral_n2i-claude-agentic: train_n=200, val_n=6, batch_size=1, grad_clip=1.0, seed=42, warm_start=True, pretrain_epochs=3, n_iter=800, outer_wall_s=1200, lr=0.0023, proj_n_bf=1, img_n_bf=7, proj_kernel=7, img_kernel=5, proj_sx=1.0, proj_sy=2.0, proj_sr=0.02, img_sx=1.5, img_sy=1.5, img_sr=0.02, rationale=iter-7: ONE knob changed vs iter-6 (n_iter 400->800, the per-scan Adam fit budget); all 18 other fields held IDENTICAL to demo_dl_dual_domain_bilateral_n2i_iter_06.json (img_n_bf=7, img_sr=0.02 LOOSE demo-correct). CEILING-DOC PROBE, not another smoothing knob. Trajectory by HEADROOM (the campaign primary metric, PSNR/noise-sensitive on demo): iter-1 img_n_bf=1 hr 0.2763 (PSNR 19.47); iter-2 n_bf=3 hr 0.3276 (+0.051); iter-3 n_bf=5 hr 0.3335 (+0.006, depth HR-BEST); iter-4 img_sr->0.0005 hr 0.1998 REGRESSED; iter-5 img_sr->0.02 revert hr 0.3320 recovered; iter-6 n_bf=7 hr 0.3330 (+0.000 vs n_bf=5, SSIM +0.009 0.7705->0.7796 but hr DEAD FLAT). FAILURE MODE: the image-domain DEPTH lever (img_n_bf) has hit its HEADROOM ceiling -- depth still lifts the SSIM structural term but its hr slope collapsed to zero by n_bf=5 (slope +0.051 -> +0.006 -> 0.000). img_sr is exhausted and substrate-confirmed wrong-direction (demo wants LOOSE 0.02; tightening collapses hr). proj_n_bf is in the symmetry trap (near-identity proj sigmas -> wasted params). So all the SMOOTHING/CAPACITY axes are exhausted on hr. The remaining open question for the ceiling claim is OPTIMIZATION budget: is hr ~0.333 the half-view FBP noise-floor bound (structural), or is the per-scan Adam fit simply stopping short at n_iter=400? Per the per-image N2I knob insights (mayo_campaign_state.md): U-Net N2I OVERFITS each scan as n_iter rises (no early-stop -> demo-n2i 0.4785->0.4293 @n_iter1200), but the 6-param BILATERAL physically CANNOT overfit one scan -- so doubling its per-scan budget is the clean diagnostic the U-Net could not give: more steps either (a) lift hr -> the plateau was under-optimization, the lever is n_iter (and lr), not depth; or (b) leave hr flat at ~0.333 -> CONFIRMS the structural half-view FBP ceiling, after which iter-8+ should stop tuning and document the ceiling with a seed/pretrain_epochs invariance probe toward iter-20. Chose n_iter over (a) img_n_bf 7->9 (depth lever's hr slope is already zero -- a 4th depth step re-confirms iter-6 with near-zero EV on hr), (b) lr (would confound the budget question -- vary n_iter first at the proven lr=2.3e-3, then lr if n_iter moves hr), (c) img_kernel/img_sx/img_sy (less-informed smoothing guesses, no hr evidence). Held fixed at iter-6 values: img_n_bf=7, img_sr=0.02, proj_n_bf=1, kernels (proj_k=7/img_k=5), proj sigmas (1.0/2.0/0.02), img spatial sigmas (img_sx=1.5/img_sy=1.5), lr=2.3e-3, warm_start=True, pretrain_epochs=3, train_n=200, val_n=6, grad_clip=1.0, seed=42 (-> identical val split, directly comparable to iter-1..6). Wall: iter-6 ran ~260 s; doubling the per-scan fit roughly doubles the per-image loop to ~450-520 s, still well under the 1800 s sbatch wall and the 1200 s outer_wall_s internal guard (under the 15-min budget). Hypothesis: hr stays ~0.333 even at n_iter=800 -- the 6-param bilateral cannot overfit and has already converged on the half-view FBP noise floor, so more fit budget yields no hr -> CONFIRMS demo bilateral N2I is at its structural ~hr 0.33 ceiling toward iter-20. If instead hr rises meaningfully (>+0.005), the plateau was optimizer-budget-limited and n_iter (then lr) becomes the live lever. PER-IMAGE bilateral N2I, AGENT4CT_DATASET=phantoms; do NOT revert to amortized.

rationale: dual_domain_bilateral_n2i-claude-agentic: train_n=200, val_n=6, batch_size=1, grad_clip=1.0, seed=42, warm_start=True, pretrain_epochs=3, n_iter=400, outer_wall_s=1200, lr=0.0023, proj_n_bf=1, img_n_bf=5, proj_kernel=7, img_kernel=5, proj_sx=1.0, proj_sy=2.0, proj_sr=0.02, img_sx=1.5, img_sy=1.5, img_sr=0.02, rationale=iter-5: ONE knob changed vs iter-4 (img_sr 0.0005->0.02, the image-domain BILATERAL RANGE sigma); all 18 other fields held IDENTICAL to demo_dl_dual_domain_bilateral_n2i_iter_04.json -> this exactly RESTORES the iter-3 config (img_n_bf=5, img_sr=0.02), the hr-best of the whole run. UNDOING THE iter-4 REGRESSION. Trajectory: iter-1 img_n_bf=1 val 0.6657/hr+0.2763/PSNR 19.47; iter-2 img_n_bf=3 val 0.7465/hr+0.3276/PSNR 20.10; iter-3 img_n_bf=5 val 0.7705/hr+0.3335/PSNR 20.18 (HR-BEST); iter-4 tightened img_sr 0.02->0.0005 -> SSIM ticked up to 0.7709 but hr COLLAPSED 0.3335->0.1998 and PSNR fell 20.18->18.60. Failure mode: tight img_sr is the WRONG lever for demo's substrate. The mayo_campaign_state.md 'tighten img_sr->0.0005 for edge preservation' insight is BREAST-specific (tight=good on dense fibroglandular breast); on demo's sparse ellipse phantoms the tight range sigma OVER-SHARPENS - it forces the 5-deep image cascade to act only across hard intensity jumps and stop smoothing the broad noise floor, so noise/PSNR worsens (20.18->18.60 dB) even though the SSIM structural term inches up. headroom is the campaign's primary structurally-bounded score and it is PSNR/noise-sensitive here, so the over-sharpen is net-negative. The img_sr lever is SUBSTRATE-SPECIFIC and OPPOSITE between breast (tight=good) and demo (loose=good). Reverting img_sr 0.0005->0.02 restores the iter-3 hr-0.3335 regime, where the loose range sigma lets the deep cascade do its proven coarse-to-fine NOISE smoothing (the demo lever that earned hr 0.276->0.328->0.335 via img_n_bf 1->3->5 at img_sr=0.02). Chose the clean SINGLE-numeric-knob revert (img_sr only) over also pushing img_n_bf 5->7 in the same iter, to first cleanly RECOVER hr 0.3335 and re-confirm the loose-img_sr regime before iter-6 pushes the proven depth lever further. Held fixed at the iter-3/iter-4 values: img_n_bf=5, proj_n_bf=1, kernels (proj_k=7/img_k=5), proj sigmas (1.0/2.0/0.02), img spatial sigmas (img_sx=1.5/img_sy=1.5), lr=2.3e-3, warm_start=True, pretrain_epochs=3, n_iter=400, train_n=200, val_n=6, grad_clip=1.0, seed=42 (-> identical val split, directly comparable to iter-1/2/3/4). Wall: iter-4 ran 264 s; img_sr is an init value, zero added compute, so wall ~unchanged, comfortably under the 1800 s sbatch wall and the 1200 s outer_wall_s guard. Hypothesis: reverting the image-domain range sigma to the looser 0.02 undoes the iter-4 over-sharpen and recovers val_score/hr to ~iter-3 (SSIM ~0.7705, hr ~0.3335, PSNR ~20.18), confirming that on demo's substrate loose img_sr is correct (opposite to breast). If hr does NOT recover to ~0.3335, it would mean the iter-4 regression was NOT purely the img_sr lever (re-examine seed/split determinism) - but per the identical-split protocol it should land back on iter-3.

rationale: dual_domain_bilateral_n2i-claude-agentic: train_n=200, val_n=6, batch_size=1, grad_clip=1.0, seed=42, warm_start=True, pretrain_epochs=3, n_iter=400, outer_wall_s=1200, lr=0.0023, proj_n_bf=1, img_n_bf=5, proj_kernel=7, img_kernel=5, proj_sx=1.0, proj_sy=2.0, proj_sr=0.02, img_sx=1.5, img_sy=1.5, img_sr=0.0005, rationale=iter-4: ONE knob changed vs iter-3 (img_sr 0.02->0.0005, the image-domain BILATERAL RANGE sigma); all 18 other fields held IDENTICAL to demo_dl_dual_domain_bilateral_n2i_iter_03.json (img_n_bf=5 deep cascade kept). PIVOT from DEPTH to RANGE-SIGMA TUNING, because depth is now in clear diminishing returns and PSNR has SATURATED. Trajectory: iter-1 img_n_bf=1 val 0.6657/hr+0.2763/PSNR 19.47; iter-2 img_n_bf=3 val 0.7465/hr+0.3276/PSNR 20.10 (+0.081 SSIM, +0.63 dB); iter-3 img_n_bf=5 val 0.7705/hr+0.3335/PSNR 20.18 (+0.024 SSIM, only +0.08 dB). The SSIM deltas are halving each depth step (+0.081 -> +0.024) and PSNR has flatlined (20.10 -> 20.18) -> img_n_bf depth has hit its structural ceiling; one more notch (5->7) would buy <0.012 SSIM at best. The higher-EV move is to make the deep 5-layer cascade we ALREADY have actually edge-preserving. Per docs/runs/mayo_campaign_state.md 'N2I PER-IMAGE knob insights' (confirmed cross-run 2026-06-18/19): on breast/demo (128-view substrates) the IMAGE-domain over-smoothing lever is img_sr, and 'default 0.02 too loose -> degenerates to a Gaussian blur ... Tighten img_sr->0.0005 for edge preservation'. The whole 5-deep cascade currently initialises every layer's RANGE sigma at 0.02, so each of the 5 BFs starts in the loose-Gaussian regime that smooths across phantom edges -> caps SSIM. Tightening img_sr to 0.0005 makes all 5 layers edge-preserving from init (sigma_r << data range preserves edges; sigma_r >> range degenerates to Gaussian, per solver_dual_ddomain_bilateral_n2i.md). This maximally leverages the deep cascade (5 layers x tighter range) and targets exactly the SSIM-capping over-smoothing rather than the exhausted PSNR/noise axis. Chose img_sr over img_n_bf 5->7 (exhausted lever, flat PSNR) and over img_kernel (a less-informed guess: kernel sets spatial extent, but the symptom here is range-domain over-smoothing across edges, which img_sr governs directly). Held fixed: img_n_bf=5, proj_n_bf=1, kernels (proj_k=7/img_k=5), proj sigmas (1.0/2.0/0.02), img spatial sigmas (img_sx=1.5/img_sy=1.5), lr=2.3e-3, warm_start=True, pretrain_epochs=3, n_iter=400, train_n=200, val_n=6, grad_clip=1.0, seed=42 (-> identical val split, directly comparable to iter-1/2/3). Wall: iter-3 ran 235 s; img_sr is an init value, zero added compute, so wall ~unchanged, comfortably under the 1800 s sbatch wall and 1200 s outer_wall_s guard. Hypothesis: tightening the image-domain range sigma to 0.0005 stops the 5-deep cascade from degenerating into a Gaussian blur across phantom edges, preserving fine structural detail and lifting val_score above iter-3's 0.7705 (the SSIM/edge axis, which still has headroom, not the saturated PSNR/noise axis). If it does NOT move val_score (or regresses), it confirms the image-domain BF range sigma is already effectively tight after training on this substrate and the next iter should pivot to img_kernel (spatial extent) or img spatial sigmas.

rationale: dual_domain_n2i-claude-agentic: train_n=200, val_n=6, batch_size=1, grad_clip=1.0, seed=42, warm_start=True, pretrain_epochs=3, n_iter=600, outer_wall_s=1200, lr=0.0001, unet_c=16, rationale=iter-3: ONE knob -> per-scan lr 1e-3 -> 1e-4 (10x lower). DIAGNOSIS (numbers, not pixels): the plateau is NOT under-convergence. iter-1 (n_iter=400) PSNR 16.13/SSIM 0.4785; iter-2 (n_iter=1200, 3x steps) PSNR 15.99/SSIM 0.4293 -> tripling per-scan steps made it STRICTLY WORSE. A fit approaching its FBP-bounded optimum would rise or plateau; it DEGRADES, the signature of the 0.466 M-param U-Net OVERFITTING each single noisy scan's split-view N2I objective. The per-image loop has no early-stop/best-iter pick (solver _fit_one_scene takes the FINAL predict after a fixed n_iter), so extra Adam steps at lr=1e-3 walk the recon away from the decent warm-start init toward a noise-fitting minimum BELOW the 16.67 dB LD-FBP baseline (hr=0). FAILURE MODE = per-image overfitting of an over-parameterized denoiser to one noisy scan. PROOF the warm-start+per-image plumbing is fine: the BILATERAL twin (identical pipeline, identical warm_start/n_iter=400/seed=42 -> SAME 6 val scenes) hit PSNR 19.47/SSIM 0.6657 hr+0.2763 at its iter-1 and climbed to 0.7465 -- its 6-12-param BF physically CANNOT overfit a single scan, which is exactly why it clears baseline while the U-Net dives under. So the lever is NOT n_iter (saturated/counterproductive) and NOT unet_c (the solver design doc explicitly warns 'don't waste iters on U-Net width: capacity is not the lever for this loss on this dataset'; the BF gained from capacity because BF capacity is structurally constrained, the U-Net's is not). The lever is the per-scan STEP SIZE: drop lr 10x to 1e-4 so Adam stays anchored near the warm-start init (the good operating point the BF twin proves exists) instead of descending into the single-scan noise-fitting minimum. n_iter trimmed 1200 -> 600 (less overshoot needed at low lr; keeps wall short). HYPOTHESIS: at lr=1e-4 the per-image fit barely moves off warm-start, so SSIM/PSNR rise toward and above the 16.67 dB LD-FBP baseline (target: break the 0.4785 plateau, ideally approach the BF twin's ~0.66 / the historical demo_dl N2I hr 0.3811); if SSIM is still flat at ~0.47 the warm-start init itself is the floor and iter-4 should toggle warm_start / raise pretrain_epochs. WALL: warm 3x200=600 + per-image 6x600=3600 = 4200 steps @ ~0.083 s/step ~= 350 s (iter-1 was 250s at 3000 steps), well under the 15-min target, the outer_wall_s=1200 guard, and the 1800 s sbatch wall. All other knobs IDENTICAL to iter-2 (train_n=200, val_n=6, batch_size=1, grad_clip=1.0, seed=42, warm_start=True, pretrain_epochs=3, unet_c=16).

Trajectory: iter-1 img_n_bf=1 -> val 0.6657 / hr +0.2763; iter-2 img_n_bf=3 -> val 0.7465 / hr +0.3276 (+0.081 SSIM, +0.63 dB PSNR). The image-domain capacity lever is the WORKING lever (proj side is in the symmetry trap per the design doc: proj sigmas near-identity -> stacked proj BFs stay locked-symmetric, so proj_n_bf stays 1). Keep exploiting the proven lever one notch further: deepen the image-domain bilateral cascade 3->5. Per solver_dual_ddomain_bilateral_n2i.md, the image-domain stack readily differentiates into a multi-scale cascade (BF1 mild + tight sigma_r, BF2 wider, BF3 widest); two MORE BFs give the cascade two additional scales (coarse-to-fine edge-preserving), growing the image denoiser from 9 to 15 trainable scalars (total network 12->18, still ultra-low, far too few to memorise 6 val scenes). Chose DEPTH over kernel/sigma because depth is the proven lever here (+0.08 with one notch 1->3) whereas a kernel/sigma tweak would be a less-informed guess. Held fixed: proj_n_bf=1, kernels (proj_k=7/img_k=5), all six sigma inits (proj 1.0/2.0/0.02, img 1.5/1.5/0.02), lr=2.3e-3, warm_start=True, pretrain_epochs=3, n_iter=400, train_n=200, val_n=6, grad_clip=1.0, seed=42 (-> identical val split, directly comparable to iter-1/iter-2). Wall: iter-2 ran 175 s; two more image-domain BFs add only a small fraction of the 128-view FBP+proj per-step cost, so comfortably under the 1800 s sbatch wall and the 1200 s outer_wall_s internal guard. Hypothesis: a 5-deep image-domain cascade adds coarse+fine scales beyond the 3-deep cascade, lifting val_score above iter-2 0.7465. If it does NOT move val_score (or regresses), the image-domain BF depth has hit its structural ceiling on this dense phantom substrate and iter-4 should pivot from DEPTH to img kernel (img_k 5->7) or img sigma tuning.
